source.title: Ulster Herald, 19 April 1924, p. 5 ("Partitionist 'triumph' in Tyrone: nominations for county and rural councils"); Belfast News-Letter, 16 April 1924, p. 10 ("Tyrone local boards: Unionists in power; nominations for Tyrone County Council")
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: the Ulster Herald list is headed 'The following nominated for the Co. Council were returned unopposed' (19 April 1924, p. 5); no contest and no withdrawal is reported for any of these divisions.

note: Poll fixed for Wednesday 28 May 1924 (Belfast News-Letter, 16 April 1924, p. 10: the county elections 'were fixed to take place on Wednesday, 28th May next'). The Nationalists abstained, so no poll was needed: the Ulster Herald (19 April 1924, p. 5) prints these nineteen divisions as 'returned unopposed' and names six more divisions - Ballygowley [Ballygawley], Carrickmore, Coagh, Dromode [Dromore], Plumbridge and Pomeroy - for which 'no nominations were received'. Cookstown and Dungannon, which are divisions in the council's later rounds, appear in neither the Belfast News-Letter list of 16 April nor the Ulster Herald list. Nineteen candidates were therefore returned unopposed and six seats were left vacant. The News-Letter's column is physically trimmed at the left edge of the microfilm (every line loses its first few characters), so the Ulster Herald printing, which gives the same names with addresses, was used to read the list. Source corrected: the News-Letter column (BNL 16 Apr 1924 p10) is physically trimmed at the microfilm edge and cannot yield complete names; the list was read from the Ulster Herald 19 Apr 1924 p5, which is now the cited source and the News-Letter the corroboration. Returned unopposed.
